    • 1. 1. Purpose and Scope
    • GHOST-SRS-FILE-TREE
      2.8.1. Requirement File Tree Parent Anchor GHOST-SRS-FILE-TREE This requirement is the parent anchor for the approved StrictDoc child-file tree. Connected child dummy files shall reference this UID, or a child-file parent UID, through StrictDoc parent references so generated HTML can display navigable requirement relationships.
    GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ROOT
    1.1. Document Retrieval and Reranking Scope GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ROOT GHOST shall retrieve query-relevant document chunks from an active project, optionally apply SPLADE and ColBERT ranking branches, hydrate selected chunks from raw sources, and write ordered candidate state into SuperPrompt for A3 evidence selection.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PRODUCT-NAME
      1.2. Product and Package Naming Boundary GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PRODUCT-NAME The product described by this document shall be named GHOST; current Python paths may remain under ragstream.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-KM-PARENT
      1.3. Retrieval Knowledge Management Parent GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-KM-PARENT Document Retrieval and Reranking shall be governed by the capability boundaries, shared artifacts, configuration governance, and sibling ownership defined in 40_knowledge_management.sdoc.

      This document shall refine the retrieval/reranking sub-capability without redefining ingestion, A3, A4, or Memory Management.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-BOUNDARY
      1.4. Retrieval Boundary GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-BOUNDARY This document shall own query projection consumption, query splitting, dense ranking, SPLADE rescoring, reciprocal-rank fusion, hydration, retrieval-stage write-back, optional ColBERT reranking, and reranked-stage write-back.

      It shall not own ingestion, A3 usefulness decisions, A4 condensation, memory retrieval, or final prompt composition.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-COMPONENTS
      1.5. Current Retrieval Components GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-COMPONENTS The current capability shall be organized around Retriever, RetrieverEmb, RetrieverSplade, rrf_merge, smart_query_splitter, Chunk hydration, and Reranker.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SP
      2.1. SuperPrompt Input GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SP Retriever shall receive the active prepared SuperPrompt, active project name, requested top_k, and SPLADE enable/bypass choice.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-PROJECTOR
        2.2. Query Projection Source GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-PROJECTOR Retriever shall obtain document query text through SuperPromptProjector.build_query_text.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ROUTING
          2.3. ActiveBrief Routing Compliance GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ROUTING The query text used for retrieval shall reflect the finalized prompt-materiality/topic-relation policy established by PreProcessing.
          • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMPTY-SUPPRESSION
            2.4. Empty Query Suppression GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMPTY-SUPPRESSION A deliberately empty document query produced by the routing policy shall suppress document retrieval and shall not be replaced by prompt_ready, memory context, or an unrelated fallback.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PROJECT
        2.5. Project Name GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PROJECT The project name shall be non-empty and shall identify one project-specific dense store and raw-document subtree.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-TOPK
        2.6. Requested Candidate Limit GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-TOPK The requested top_k shall define the maximum fused retrieval rows returned by the retrieval stage when positive.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-NO-MEMORY-QUERY
        2.7. No Memory Query Ownership GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-NO-MEMORY-QUERY Document Retriever shall not query the memory vector store or MemoryIndexLookup.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-SPLIT
      3.1. Query Piece Generation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-SPLIT The projected query shall be split into ordered overlapping text pieces before dense and sparse scoring.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-TRIM
        3.2. Query Trim GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-TRIM Query splitting shall trim the complete query and shall return an empty list when no usable text remains.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-CHUNKER
        3.3. Shared Chunker Use GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-CHUNKER The current query splitter shall reuse the deterministic Chunker windowing algorithm.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-SIZE
        3.4. Query Window Validation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-SIZE Query chunk size shall be positive; overlap shall be non-negative and smaller than chunk size.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-BASELINE
        3.5. Current Query Window Baseline GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-BASELINE The current query-splitting baseline shall use 1200-character windows with 120-character overlap until replaced by approved runtime configuration.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-ORDER
        3.6. Query Piece Order GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-ORDER Returned query pieces shall preserve the order produced by deterministic windowing and shall exclude empty pieces.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-NO-SMART-CLAIM
        3.7. No Semantic Splitter Claim GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-NO-SMART-CLAIM The current smart_query_splitter module shall not be described as semantic, sentence-aware, or LLM-based while its implementation remains linear character windowing.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-FIRST
      4.1. Dense First-Pass Retrieval GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-FIRST RetrieverEmb shall generate the initial candidate set from the active project Chroma document store.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-NEUTRAL
        4.2. Dense Backend State Neutrality GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-NEUTRAL RetrieverEmb shall receive project name, query pieces, and top_k without knowledge of SuperPrompt write-back or raw-file hydration.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-STORE
        4.3. Dense Store Validation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-STORE Dense retrieval shall fail explicitly when the Chroma root or active project store does not exist.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-EMPTY-QUERY
        4.4. Dense Empty Query GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-EMPTY-QUERY Dense retrieval shall return no rows when query pieces are empty.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-READ
        4.5. Dense Store Read Contract GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-READ Dense retrieval shall read stored chunk identifiers, embeddings, and metadata from the active project collection.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-LENGTH
        4.6. Dense Store Shape Validation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-LENGTH Dense retrieval shall reject mismatched identifier/embedding lengths and mismatched non-empty metadata lengths.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-QUERY-EMBED
        4.7. Query Embedding GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-QUERY-EMBED The dense backend shall embed all query pieces using the configured dense Embedder.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-DIM
        4.8. Embedding Dimension Validation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-DIM Stored and query embedding matrices shall be two-dimensional and shall have equal vector dimensions.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-COSINE
        4.9. Cosine Similarity GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-COSINE The dense backend shall row-normalize stored and query vectors and shall compute cosine similarities by matrix multiplication.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PNORM
        4.10. Query-Piece Aggregation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PNORM Per-chunk dense similarities across query pieces shall be clipped at zero and aggregated by p-norm mean.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PNORM-P
          4.11. Current Dense p Value GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PNORM-P The current dense p-norm aggregation baseline shall use p = 10 until replaced by approved configuration.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-SORT
        4.12. Dense Deterministic Sort GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-SORT Dense rows shall be ordered by descending aggregated score and then ascending chunk identifier for ties.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-CUTOFF
        4.13. Dense Candidate Cutoff GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-CUTOFF Dense retrieval shall return no more than the positive requested top_k or its documented fallback when the caller supplies no valid positive limit.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR
        5.1. Hard Dense Similarity Floor GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR Retriever shall remove dense candidate rows whose dense score is below the configured hard_embedding_floor.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR-ZERO
          5.2. Disabled Floor GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR-ZERO A non-positive hard_embedding_floor shall disable dense-floor filtering.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR-SOURCE
          5.3. Floor Configuration Source GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR-SOURCE The current hard embedding floor shall be read from runtime_config.document_retrieval.hard_embedding_floor.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR-META
          5.4. Floor Score Meaning GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR-META The score compared to hard_embedding_floor shall be the aggregated dense embedding score later projected as emb_score.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-FLOOR
          14.4. AC: Hard Floor GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-FLOOR Given a positive hard embedding floor, every dense row entering SPLADE/fusion shall have dense score greater than or equal to that floor.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-DENSE
        14.3. AC: Dense Ranking GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-DENSE Given a valid project store and query pieces, dense retrieval shall return at most top_k rows ordered by p-norm aggregated cosine score with deterministic tie resolution.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-OPTION
      6.1. SPLADE Enable Switch GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-OPTION Retriever shall accept an explicit use_retrieval_splade switch.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-LAZY
        6.2. Lazy Sparse Initialization GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-LAZY The SPLADE encoder and RetrieverSplade backend shall be initialized lazily on first enabled use.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-CANDIDATES
        6.3. Dense-Bounded Sparse Candidates GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-CANDIDATES When enabled, RetrieverSplade shall score exactly the unique ordered identifiers surviving dense retrieval and hard-floor filtering.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-NOT-INDEPENDENT
          6.4. No Independent Sparse Search Claim GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-NOT-INDEPENDENT The current enabled SPLADE branch shall not be described as an independent global sparse candidate generator because it receives dense-selected candidate_ids.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-MISSING-ID
          6.6. Sparse Candidate Alignment GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-MISSING-ID Every dense-selected candidate identifier shall exist in the active SPLADE store; missing identifiers shall fail the sparse backend explicitly.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-SPARSE
          14.5. AC: Dense-Bounded SPLADE GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-SPARSE Given SPLADE enabled, every sparse-scored identifier shall belong to the dense survivor set and every dense survivor shall be present in the sparse store or the branch shall fail explicitly.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-STORE
        6.5. Sparse Store Validation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-STORE Enabled sparse retrieval shall validate the SPLADE root and active project store.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-QUERY
        6.7. Query-Side Sparse Encoding GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-QUERY RetrieverSplade shall encode query pieces using the query-side sparse encoder.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-DOT
        6.8. Sparse Similarity GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-DOT Sparse document and query representations shall be compared by deterministic sparse dot product.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-PNORM
        6.9. Sparse Piece Aggregation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-PNORM Per-chunk sparse similarities across query pieces shall be clipped at zero and aggregated by p-norm mean.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-P
          6.10. Current Sparse p Value GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-P The current sparse p-norm aggregation baseline shall use p = 10 until replaced by approved configuration.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-SORT
        6.11. Sparse Deterministic Sort GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-SORT Sparse rows shall be sorted by descending aggregated score and ascending chunk identifier for ties.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-MISSING-STORE
        6.12. Missing Sparse Store Fallback GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-MISSING-STORE When the top-level Retriever encounters FileNotFoundError for an older project without a SPLADE store, it shall continue with an empty sparse row list rather than aborting dense retrieval.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-BYPASS
        6.13. SPLADE Bypass Contract GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-BYPASS When SPLADE is disabled, Retriever shall duplicate the dense ranked rows into the second fusion input so the downstream fusion/write-back contract remains unchanged.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-SPARSE-BYPASS
          14.6. AC: SPLADE Bypass GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-SPARSE-BYPASS Given SPLADE disabled, retrieval shall complete using dense duplication as the second fusion input and shall expose bypass status.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-BYPASS-DIAG
        6.14. SPLADE Bypass Observability GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-BYPASS-DIAG The system shall expose whether SPLADE used real sparse scores, was unavailable, or was bypassed with dense duplication.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF1
      7.1. Retrieval RRF Fusion GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF1 Retriever shall fuse dense and sparse/bypass ranked lists using weighted reciprocal-rank fusion.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-K
        7.2. RRF Constant GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-K The RRF helper shall use a positive configurable rank constant; the current baseline shall be 60.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-WEIGHTS
        7.3. Current Retrieval Fusion Weights GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-WEIGHTS The current retrieval fusion baseline shall weight the dense list 0.75 and the sparse/bypass list 0.25 until replaced by approved JSON configuration.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-SCORE
        7.4. RRF Score Calculation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-SCORE Each available rank contribution shall equal its branch weight divided by RRF constant plus one-based rank; contributions shall be summed by chunk identifier.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-UNION
        7.5. RRF Identifier Union GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-UNION The neutral RRF helper shall support the union of identifiers appearing in either input list.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-META
        7.6. RRF Metadata GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-META The neutral RRF result shall preserve merged metadata and attach generic branch scores, branch ranks, and fused rrf_score when available.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-META-MERGE
        7.7. Conservative Metadata Merge GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-META-MERGE Metadata fusion shall retain an existing key value and shall add only keys absent from the accumulated metadata.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-SORT
        7.8. Fused Deterministic Sort GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-SORT Fused rows shall be ordered by descending fused score and ascending chunk identifier for ties.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-CUTOFF
        7.9. Fused Retrieval Cutoff GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-CUTOFF The retrieval RRF output shall be limited to the requested positive top_k.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-PROJECTION
        7.10. Retrieval Metadata Projection GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-PROJECTION Retriever shall map neutral RRF branch fields to retrieval-specific emb_score, splade_score, emb_rank, splade_rank, and rrf_score aliases without discarding neutral metadata.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-RRF1
        14.7. AC: First Fusion GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-RRF1 Given two ranked inputs and configured weights, fused scores and order shall match deterministic weighted RRF with the configured rank constant.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE
      8.1. Hydration Requirement GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE Retriever shall hydrate each fused ranked row into a Chunk object before writing request-time document context into SuperPrompt.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-PATH
        8.2. Hydration Source Path GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-PATH Hydration shall resolve metadata path relative to the configured document root.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-INDEX
        8.3. Hydration Chunk Index GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-INDEX Hydration shall require chunk_idx metadata and shall select the corresponding reconstructed chunk.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-SAME-CONFIG
        8.4. Hydration Chunking Consistency GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-SAME-CONFIG Hydration shall use the same effective chunk size and overlap as ingestion for the source-version being reconstructed.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-CACHE
        8.5. Per-Run Hydration Cache GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-CACHE Hydration shall cache source text and reconstructed chunk lists per source path within one retrieval run to avoid repeated reads and splits.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-SKIP-PATH
        8.6. Broken Path Skip GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-SKIP-PATH A ranked row with missing path metadata or a missing raw source file shall be skipped rather than crashing hydration of all other rows.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-SKIP-IDX
        8.7. Broken Index Skip GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-SKIP-IDX A ranked row with absent, negative, or out-of-range chunk index shall be skipped rather than becoming a fabricated chunk.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-ALIGN
        8.8. Hydrated Row Alignment GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-ALIGN The list of valid ranked rows and hydrated Chunk objects shall remain one-to-one and order-aligned.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-HYDRATE
          14.8. AC: Hydration GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-HYDRATE Every row written to the retrieval view shall have a corresponding hydrated Chunk; broken rows shall be omitted from both aligned outputs.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CHUNK-CONTRACT
        8.9. Chunk Runtime Contract GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CHUNK-CONTRACT A hydrated Chunk shall contain stable identifier, project-relative source, snippet, reconstructed source span, and copied metadata.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-NO-MUTATE
        8.10. Hydration Source Integrity GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-NO-MUTATE Hydration shall read source files and shall not modify the raw project document or persistent vector metadata.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-WRITE
      9.1. Retrieval Write-Back GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-WRITE Retriever shall write valid hydrated chunks and ordered ranking state into the same SuperPrompt.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-BASE
        9.2. Base Context Chunks GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-BASE sp.base_context_chunks shall contain hydrated chunks in fused retrieval order.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-VIEW
        9.3. Retrieval View GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-VIEW sp.views_by_stage["retrieval"] shall contain ordered triples of chunk identifier, retrieval fused score, and SELECTED status.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PASSTHROUGH
        9.4. A3-Ready Passthrough View GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PASSTHROUGH Retrieval shall initialize sp.views_by_stage["reranked"] as a copy of retrieval ordering and scores so A3 can run when real ColBERT reranking is not executed.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PASSTHROUGH-NOT-RERANK
          9.5. Passthrough Truthfulness GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PASSTHROUGH-NOT-RERANK The retrieval-created reranked view shall be marked as passthrough and shall not be represented as a completed ColBERT ranking.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-PASSTHROUGH
          14.9. AC: Retrieval Passthrough GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-PASSTHROUGH After retrieval without real reranking, the reranked view shall equal the retrieval view and diagnostics shall identify retrieval_passthrough.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-FINAL-IDS
        9.6. Retrieval Final IDs GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-FINAL-IDS sp.final_selection_ids shall equal the ordered identifiers of the valid hydrated retrieval rows.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-STAGE
        9.7. Retrieval Lifecycle GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-STAGE After successful retrieval write-back, sp.stage shall equal retrieval and history_of_stages shall receive retrieval.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DIAG
        9.8. Retrieval Passthrough Diagnostics GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DIAG SuperPrompt extras shall record the A3-ready source, candidate count, and reranked passthrough state.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-ROOT
      10.1. Reranker Capability GHOST-DOC-RERANK-ROOT Reranker shall optionally rescore and reorder the bounded document candidates already stored by Retrieval.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-PRECONDITION
        10.2. Reranker Preconditions GHOST-DOC-RERANK-PRECONDITION Reranker shall require a non-empty retrieval view and non-empty base_context_chunks.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-QUERY
        10.3. Reranker Query Projection GHOST-DOC-RERANK-QUERY Real reranking shall rebuild the current query text through SuperPromptProjector and split it with the configured query-window contract.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CANDIDATE-CAP
        10.4. Reranker Candidate Cap GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CANDIDATE-CAP Real or bypass reranking shall process no more than the effective reranker top_k candidates; the current constructor baseline shall be 50.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-MODEL
        10.5. Current ColBERT Model GHOST-DOC-RERANK-MODEL The current reranker model baseline shall be lightonai/GTE-ModernColBERT-v1 until changed by approved configuration.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-DEVICE
        10.6. Reranker Device Governance GHOST-DOC-RERANK-DEVICE The reranker runtime device shall be configurable and shall be honored by model initialization.

        The current constructor default of cpu shall not be claimed as enforced when the backend model is created without applying the device argument.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-DYNAMIC
        10.7. Dynamic Cleaning Only GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-DYNAMIC Reranker shall clean a temporary scoring copy of each chunk text and shall not alter the stored or hydrated canonical snippet.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-FRONT
          10.8. Front-Matter Cleaning GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-FRONT Reranker cleaning shall remove an initial delimited front-matter block when present.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-META
          10.9. Metadata-Line Cleaning GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-META Reranker cleaning shall remove configured line-level metadata keys such as title, author, version, updated, tags, dates, and description.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-ARTIFACT
          10.10. Prompt-Artifact Cleaning GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-ARTIFACT Reranker cleaning shall remove code-fence marker lines, @@meta lines, and recognized END_OF_PROMPT marker lines while preserving normal content.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-EMPTY
          10.11. Empty Cleaned Candidate GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-EMPTY A candidate whose cleaned scoring text is empty shall be excluded from ColBERT scoring.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-CLEAN
          14.12. AC: Non-Mutating Cleaning GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-CLEAN Reranker cleaning shall alter only the temporary scoring text; the corresponding base_context_chunks snippets shall remain unchanged.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-NO-VALID
        10.12. No Valid Rerank Candidates GHOST-DOC-RERANK-NO-VALID Real reranking shall fail explicitly when no candidate can be prepared for ColBERT scoring.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-ENCODE
        11.1. ColBERT Encoding GHOST-DOC-RERANK-ENCODE Real reranking shall encode query pieces as queries and the cleaned candidate snippets as documents using the configured ColBERT model.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-DOCS-PER-QUERY
          11.2. Candidate Set per Query Piece GHOST-DOC-RERANK-DOCS-PER-QUERY Every query piece shall be scored against the same ordered valid candidate identifier and document list.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-MEAN
          11.3. ColBERT Piece Aggregation GHOST-DOC-RERANK-MEAN For each chunk identifier, ColBERT scores returned across query pieces shall be aggregated by arithmetic mean.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-COLBERT-SORT
          11.4. ColBERT Deterministic Sort GHOST-DOC-RERANK-COLBERT-SORT Aggregated ColBERT rows shall be ordered by descending mean score and ascending chunk identifier for ties.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-RRF2
        11.5. Second Weighted RRF GHOST-DOC-RERANK-RRF2 Reranker shall fuse the original retrieval ranking with the ColBERT ranking through the same neutral weighted RRF helper.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-WEIGHTS
          11.6. Current Reranker Fusion Weights GHOST-DOC-RERANK-WEIGHTS The current second-fusion baseline shall weight Retrieval 0.75 and ColBERT 0.25.

          Comments describing equal weighting shall not override the executed values.
          • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-WEIGHTS
            14.13. AC: Executed Weight Truth GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-WEIGHTS The effective retrieval and reranking weights reported for the current baseline shall be 0.75/0.25 unless validated JSON configuration overrides them in implemented code.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-META-PRESERVE
          11.7. Retrieval Metadata Preservation GHOST-DOC-RERANK-META-PRESERVE Before the second fusion overwrites generic rrf_score, the original retrieval fused score shall be preserved under retrieval_rrf_score when available.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-META-PROJECT
          11.8. Reranker Metadata Projection GHOST-DOC-RERANK-META-PROJECT Reranker shall project neutral second-fusion fields to retrieval_score, colbert_score, retrieval_rank, colbert_rank, and rerank_rrf_score.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-WRITE-META
          11.9. Chunk Metadata Write-Back GHOST-DOC-RERANK-WRITE-META Reranker-specific scores and ranks shall be merged into the hydrated chunk metadata for later diagnostic rendering.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-FINAL-SORT
          11.10. Final Rerank Order GHOST-DOC-RERANK-FINAL-SORT The final reranked rows shall be sorted by descending rerank fused score and ascending chunk identifier for ties.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-COLBERT
          14.10. AC: ColBERT Reranking GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-COLBERT Given real reranking enabled and valid candidates, ColBERT mean scores shall be fused with retrieval ranking using the configured second-fusion values and shall produce the reranked view.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-BYPASS
        12.1. ColBERT Bypass GHOST-DOC-RERANK-BYPASS When use_reranking_colbert is false, Reranker shall copy the bounded retrieval order and scores into the reranked stage without calling the ColBERT model.
        • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-BYPASS-META
          12.2. Bypass Metadata GHOST-DOC-RERANK-BYPASS-META Bypass may populate retrieval and ColBERT score/rank aliases from the retrieval order solely to preserve downstream metadata shape; diagnostics shall identify the bypass.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-RERANK-BYPASS
          14.11. AC: ColBERT Bypass GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-RERANK-BYPASS Given ColBERT disabled, no ColBERT model call shall occur and retrieval order shall be copied into the reranked stage.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-VIEW
        12.3. Reranked View GHOST-DOC-RERANK-VIEW sp.views_by_stage["reranked"] shall contain ordered chunk identifier, effective rerank score, and SELECTED status for every retained candidate.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-IDS
        12.4. Reranked Final IDs GHOST-DOC-RERANK-IDS sp.final_selection_ids shall equal the ordered identifiers in the reranked view.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-STAGE
        12.5. Reranker Lifecycle GHOST-DOC-RERANK-STAGE After real or bypass reranking, sp.stage shall equal reranked and history_of_stages shall receive reranked.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-BASE-PRESERVE
        12.6. Base Chunk Preservation GHOST-DOC-RERANK-BASE-PRESERVE Reranker shall not replace base_context_chunks; it shall reorder candidates through views and selection identifiers while enriching metadata only.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CONFIG-JSON
      13.1. JSON Configuration Target GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CONFIG-JSON Retrieval and reranking tuning parameters shall be migrated to versioned runtime_config.json.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CONFIG-FIELDS
        13.2. Retrieval Configuration Fields GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CONFIG-FIELDS The configuration target shall include query chunk size/overlap, dense model, dense p value, dense candidate limit, embedding floor, SPLADE enablement/model/device/p value, first RRF constant/weights, hydration chunk parameters, reranker model/device/candidate cap, ColBERT enablement, and second RRF constant/weights.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CONFIG-UNUSED
        13.3. Unused Current Runtime Keys GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CONFIG-UNUSED runtime_config document_retrieval keys that are not consumed by the active code, including semantic_stage_max_total_chunks or max_document_chunks_for_a3 where not wired, shall not be described as enforced runtime limits.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CONFIG-WEIGHTS
        13.4. Weight Validation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CONFIG-WEIGHTS Configured fusion weights shall be finite and non-negative and at least one branch weight shall be positive.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CONFIG-LIMITS
        13.5. Limit Validation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CONFIG-LIMITS Configured candidate limits, p values, RRF constants, and query chunk size shall be positive; overlap shall satisfy the splitter contract.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-CONFIG
        14.14. AC: JSON Parameter Migration GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-CONFIG After configuration migration, changing a retrieval limit, p value, RRF constant, branch weight, model, device, or query window shall require only validated JSON change and shall be reflected in diagnostics.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EFFECTIVE
      13.6. Effective Retrieval Diagnostics GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EFFECTIVE The run shall expose effective query-piece count, dense count, floor-survivor count, sparse mode/count, fusion weights, hydrated count, reranker mode/count, and model identifiers.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ERROR
      13.7. Retrieval Error Integrity GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ERROR Missing dense project stores, invalid vector shapes, incompatible dimensions, sparse candidate misalignment, empty reranker preparation, or invalid configuration shall not produce fabricated successful rankings.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-OPTIONAL-ERROR
      13.8. Optional Branch Failure Boundary GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-OPTIONAL-ERROR Only documented optional-branch failures may degrade to a fallback; mandatory dense retrieval and hydration-contract failures shall remain observable.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-LOG-CONTENT
      13.9. Retrieval Logging Content GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-LOG-CONTENT Normal logs shall expose stage status, counts, effective modes, model identifiers, and latency without dumping full project evidence by default.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CODE-OWNERSHIP
      14.1. Retrieval Code Ownership GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CODE-OWNERSHIP Retriever, RetrieverEmb, RetrieverSplade, rrf_merge, smart_query_splitter, Chunk, DocScore compatibility, and Reranker shall map to the deepest applicable UIDs in this document.

    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SIBLING
      14.2. Sibling Ownership Boundary GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SIBLING Document ingestion shall remain owned by 41 and A3/A4 behavior shall remain owned by 43.

    3. 3. Deterministic Query Splitting
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ROOT
      1.1. Document Retrieval and Reranking Scope GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ROOT GHOST shall retrieve query-relevant document chunks from an active project, optionally apply SPLADE and ColBERT ranking branches, hydrate selected chunks from raw sources, and write ordered candidate state into SuperPrompt for A3 evidence selection.

    GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-SPLIT
    3.1. Query Piece Generation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-SPLIT The projected query shall be split into ordered overlapping text pieces before dense and sparse scoring.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-TRIM
      3.2. Query Trim GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-TRIM Query splitting shall trim the complete query and shall return an empty list when no usable text remains.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-CHUNKER
      3.3. Shared Chunker Use GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-CHUNKER The current query splitter shall reuse the deterministic Chunker windowing algorithm.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-SIZE
      3.4. Query Window Validation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-SIZE Query chunk size shall be positive; overlap shall be non-negative and smaller than chunk size.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-BASELINE
      3.5. Current Query Window Baseline GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-BASELINE The current query-splitting baseline shall use 1200-character windows with 120-character overlap until replaced by approved runtime configuration.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-ORDER
      3.6. Query Piece Order GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-QUERY-ORDER Returned query pieces shall preserve the order produced by deterministic windowing and shall exclude empty pieces.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-NO-SMART-CLAIM
      3.7. No Semantic Splitter Claim GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-NO-SMART-CLAIM The current smart_query_splitter module shall not be described as semantic, sentence-aware, or LLM-based while its implementation remains linear character windowing.

    4. 4. Dense Candidate Generation
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ROOT
      1.1. Document Retrieval and Reranking Scope GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ROOT GHOST shall retrieve query-relevant document chunks from an active project, optionally apply SPLADE and ColBERT ranking branches, hydrate selected chunks from raw sources, and write ordered candidate state into SuperPrompt for A3 evidence selection.

        2.8.1. Requirement File Tree Parent Anchor GHOST-SRS-FILE-TREE This requirement is the parent anchor for the approved StrictDoc child-file tree. Connected child dummy files shall reference this UID, or a child-file parent UID, through StrictDoc parent references so generated HTML can display navigable requirement relationships.
    GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-FIRST
    4.1. Dense First-Pass Retrieval GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-FIRST RetrieverEmb shall generate the initial candidate set from the active project Chroma document store.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-NEUTRAL
      4.2. Dense Backend State Neutrality GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-NEUTRAL RetrieverEmb shall receive project name, query pieces, and top_k without knowledge of SuperPrompt write-back or raw-file hydration.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-STORE
      4.3. Dense Store Validation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-STORE Dense retrieval shall fail explicitly when the Chroma root or active project store does not exist.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-EMPTY-QUERY
      4.4. Dense Empty Query GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-EMPTY-QUERY Dense retrieval shall return no rows when query pieces are empty.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-READ
      4.5. Dense Store Read Contract GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-READ Dense retrieval shall read stored chunk identifiers, embeddings, and metadata from the active project collection.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-LENGTH
      4.6. Dense Store Shape Validation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-LENGTH Dense retrieval shall reject mismatched identifier/embedding lengths and mismatched non-empty metadata lengths.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-QUERY-EMBED
      4.7. Query Embedding GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-QUERY-EMBED The dense backend shall embed all query pieces using the configured dense Embedder.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-DIM
      4.8. Embedding Dimension Validation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-DIM Stored and query embedding matrices shall be two-dimensional and shall have equal vector dimensions.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-COSINE
      4.9. Cosine Similarity GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-COSINE The dense backend shall row-normalize stored and query vectors and shall compute cosine similarities by matrix multiplication.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PNORM
      4.10. Query-Piece Aggregation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PNORM Per-chunk dense similarities across query pieces shall be clipped at zero and aggregated by p-norm mean.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PNORM-P
        4.11. Current Dense p Value GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-PNORM-P The current dense p-norm aggregation baseline shall use p = 10 until replaced by approved configuration.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-SORT
      4.12. Dense Deterministic Sort GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-SORT Dense rows shall be ordered by descending aggregated score and then ascending chunk identifier for ties.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-CUTOFF
      4.13. Dense Candidate Cutoff GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-DENSE-CUTOFF Dense retrieval shall return no more than the positive requested top_k or its documented fallback when the caller supplies no valid positive limit.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR
      5.1. Hard Dense Similarity Floor GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR Retriever shall remove dense candidate rows whose dense score is below the configured hard_embedding_floor.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR-ZERO
        5.2. Disabled Floor GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR-ZERO A non-positive hard_embedding_floor shall disable dense-floor filtering.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR-SOURCE
        5.3. Floor Configuration Source GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR-SOURCE The current hard embedding floor shall be read from runtime_config.document_retrieval.hard_embedding_floor.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR-META
        5.4. Floor Score Meaning GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-EMB-FLOOR-META The score compared to hard_embedding_floor shall be the aggregated dense embedding score later projected as emb_score.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-FLOOR
        14.4. AC: Hard Floor GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-FLOOR Given a positive hard embedding floor, every dense row entering SPLADE/fusion shall have dense score greater than or equal to that floor.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-DENSE
      14.3. AC: Dense Ranking GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-DENSE Given a valid project store and query pieces, dense retrieval shall return at most top_k rows ordered by p-norm aggregated cosine score with deterministic tie resolution.

    GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-OPTION
    6.1. SPLADE Enable Switch GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-OPTION Retriever shall accept an explicit use_retrieval_splade switch.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-LAZY
      6.2. Lazy Sparse Initialization GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-LAZY The SPLADE encoder and RetrieverSplade backend shall be initialized lazily on first enabled use.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-CANDIDATES
      6.3. Dense-Bounded Sparse Candidates GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-CANDIDATES When enabled, RetrieverSplade shall score exactly the unique ordered identifiers surviving dense retrieval and hard-floor filtering.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-NOT-INDEPENDENT
        6.4. No Independent Sparse Search Claim GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-NOT-INDEPENDENT The current enabled SPLADE branch shall not be described as an independent global sparse candidate generator because it receives dense-selected candidate_ids.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-MISSING-ID
        6.6. Sparse Candidate Alignment GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-MISSING-ID Every dense-selected candidate identifier shall exist in the active SPLADE store; missing identifiers shall fail the sparse backend explicitly.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-SPARSE
        14.5. AC: Dense-Bounded SPLADE GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-SPARSE Given SPLADE enabled, every sparse-scored identifier shall belong to the dense survivor set and every dense survivor shall be present in the sparse store or the branch shall fail explicitly.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-STORE
      6.5. Sparse Store Validation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-STORE Enabled sparse retrieval shall validate the SPLADE root and active project store.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-QUERY
      6.7. Query-Side Sparse Encoding GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-QUERY RetrieverSplade shall encode query pieces using the query-side sparse encoder.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-DOT
      6.8. Sparse Similarity GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-DOT Sparse document and query representations shall be compared by deterministic sparse dot product.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-PNORM
      6.9. Sparse Piece Aggregation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-PNORM Per-chunk sparse similarities across query pieces shall be clipped at zero and aggregated by p-norm mean.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-P
        6.10. Current Sparse p Value GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-P The current sparse p-norm aggregation baseline shall use p = 10 until replaced by approved configuration.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-SORT
      6.11. Sparse Deterministic Sort GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-SORT Sparse rows shall be sorted by descending aggregated score and ascending chunk identifier for ties.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-MISSING-STORE
      6.12. Missing Sparse Store Fallback GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-MISSING-STORE When the top-level Retriever encounters FileNotFoundError for an older project without a SPLADE store, it shall continue with an empty sparse row list rather than aborting dense retrieval.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-BYPASS
      6.13. SPLADE Bypass Contract GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-BYPASS When SPLADE is disabled, Retriever shall duplicate the dense ranked rows into the second fusion input so the downstream fusion/write-back contract remains unchanged.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-SPARSE-BYPASS
        14.6. AC: SPLADE Bypass GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-SPARSE-BYPASS Given SPLADE disabled, retrieval shall complete using dense duplication as the second fusion input and shall expose bypass status.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-BYPASS-DIAG
      6.14. SPLADE Bypass Observability GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-SPARSE-BYPASS-DIAG The system shall expose whether SPLADE used real sparse scores, was unavailable, or was bypassed with dense duplication.

    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ROOT

    GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF1
    7.1. Retrieval RRF Fusion GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF1 Retriever shall fuse dense and sparse/bypass ranked lists using weighted reciprocal-rank fusion.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-K
      7.2. RRF Constant GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-K The RRF helper shall use a positive configurable rank constant; the current baseline shall be 60.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-WEIGHTS
      7.3. Current Retrieval Fusion Weights GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-WEIGHTS The current retrieval fusion baseline shall weight the dense list 0.75 and the sparse/bypass list 0.25 until replaced by approved JSON configuration.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-SCORE
      7.4. RRF Score Calculation GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-SCORE Each available rank contribution shall equal its branch weight divided by RRF constant plus one-based rank; contributions shall be summed by chunk identifier.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-UNION
      7.5. RRF Identifier Union GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-UNION The neutral RRF helper shall support the union of identifiers appearing in either input list.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-META
      7.6. RRF Metadata GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-META The neutral RRF result shall preserve merged metadata and attach generic branch scores, branch ranks, and fused rrf_score when available.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-META-MERGE
      7.7. Conservative Metadata Merge GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-META-MERGE Metadata fusion shall retain an existing key value and shall add only keys absent from the accumulated metadata.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-SORT
      7.8. Fused Deterministic Sort GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-SORT Fused rows shall be ordered by descending fused score and ascending chunk identifier for ties.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-CUTOFF
      7.9. Fused Retrieval Cutoff GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-CUTOFF The retrieval RRF output shall be limited to the requested positive top_k.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-PROJECTION
      7.10. Retrieval Metadata Projection GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-RRF-PROJECTION Retriever shall map neutral RRF branch fields to retrieval-specific emb_score, splade_score, emb_rank, splade_rank, and rrf_score aliases without discarding neutral metadata.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-RRF1

    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ROOT

Connected child dummy files shall reference this UID, or a child-file parent UID, through StrictDoc parent references so generated HTML can display navigable requirement relationships.
    GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE
    8.1. Hydration Requirement GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE Retriever shall hydrate each fused ranked row into a Chunk object before writing request-time document context into SuperPrompt.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-PATH
      8.2. Hydration Source Path GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-PATH Hydration shall resolve metadata path relative to the configured document root.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-INDEX
      8.3. Hydration Chunk Index GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-INDEX Hydration shall require chunk_idx metadata and shall select the corresponding reconstructed chunk.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-SAME-CONFIG
      8.4. Hydration Chunking Consistency GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-SAME-CONFIG Hydration shall use the same effective chunk size and overlap as ingestion for the source-version being reconstructed.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-CACHE
      8.5. Per-Run Hydration Cache GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-CACHE Hydration shall cache source text and reconstructed chunk lists per source path within one retrieval run to avoid repeated reads and splits.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-SKIP-PATH
      8.6. Broken Path Skip GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-SKIP-PATH A ranked row with missing path metadata or a missing raw source file shall be skipped rather than crashing hydration of all other rows.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-SKIP-IDX
      8.7. Broken Index Skip GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-SKIP-IDX A ranked row with absent, negative, or out-of-range chunk index shall be skipped rather than becoming a fabricated chunk.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-ALIGN
      8.8. Hydrated Row Alignment GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-ALIGN The list of valid ranked rows and hydrated Chunk objects shall remain one-to-one and order-aligned.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-HYDRATE
        14.8. AC: Hydration GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-HYDRATE Every row written to the retrieval view shall have a corresponding hydrated Chunk; broken rows shall be omitted from both aligned outputs.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CHUNK-CONTRACT
      8.9. Chunk Runtime Contract GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-CHUNK-CONTRACT A hydrated Chunk shall contain stable identifier, project-relative source, snippet, reconstructed source span, and copied metadata.
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-NO-MUTATE
      8.10. Hydration Source Integrity GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-HYDRATE-NO-MUTATE Hydration shall read source files and shall not modify the raw project document or persistent vector metadata.

    10. 10. Optional ColBERT Reranking Input and Cleaning
    • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ROOT
      1.1. Document Retrieval and Reranking Scope GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-ROOT GHOST shall retrieve query-relevant document chunks from an active project, optionally apply SPLADE and ColBERT ranking branches, hydrate selected chunks from raw sources, and write ordered candidate state into SuperPrompt for A3 evidence selection.
      • GHOST-SRS-FILE-TREE
        2.8.1. Requirement File Tree Parent Anchor GHOST-SRS-FILE-TREE This requirement is the parent anchor for the approved StrictDoc child-file tree. Connected child dummy files shall reference this UID, or a child-file parent UID, through StrictDoc parent references so generated HTML can display navigable requirement relationships.
    GHOST-DOC-RERANK-ROOT
    10.1. Reranker Capability GHOST-DOC-RERANK-ROOT Reranker shall optionally rescore and reorder the bounded document candidates already stored by Retrieval.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-PRECONDITION
      10.2. Reranker Preconditions GHOST-DOC-RERANK-PRECONDITION Reranker shall require a non-empty retrieval view and non-empty base_context_chunks.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-QUERY
      10.3. Reranker Query Projection GHOST-DOC-RERANK-QUERY Real reranking shall rebuild the current query text through SuperPromptProjector and split it with the configured query-window contract.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CANDIDATE-CAP
      10.4. Reranker Candidate Cap GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CANDIDATE-CAP Real or bypass reranking shall process no more than the effective reranker top_k candidates; the current constructor baseline shall be 50.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-MODEL
      10.5. Current ColBERT Model GHOST-DOC-RERANK-MODEL The current reranker model baseline shall be lightonai/GTE-ModernColBERT-v1 until changed by approved configuration.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-DEVICE
      10.6. Reranker Device Governance GHOST-DOC-RERANK-DEVICE The reranker runtime device shall be configurable and shall be honored by model initialization.

      The current constructor default of cpu shall not be claimed as enforced when the backend model is created without applying the device argument.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-DYNAMIC
      10.7. Dynamic Cleaning Only GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-DYNAMIC Reranker shall clean a temporary scoring copy of each chunk text and shall not alter the stored or hydrated canonical snippet.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-FRONT
        10.8. Front-Matter Cleaning GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-FRONT Reranker cleaning shall remove an initial delimited front-matter block when present.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-META
        10.9. Metadata-Line Cleaning GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-META Reranker cleaning shall remove configured line-level metadata keys such as title, author, version, updated, tags, dates, and description.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-ARTIFACT
        10.10. Prompt-Artifact Cleaning GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-ARTIFACT Reranker cleaning shall remove code-fence marker lines, @@meta lines, and recognized END_OF_PROMPT marker lines while preserving normal content.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-EMPTY
        10.11. Empty Cleaned Candidate GHOST-DOC-RERANK-CLEAN-EMPTY A candidate whose cleaned scoring text is empty shall be excluded from ColBERT scoring.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-CLEAN
        14.12. AC: Non-Mutating Cleaning GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-CLEAN Reranker cleaning shall alter only the temporary scoring text; the corresponding base_context_chunks snippets shall remain unchanged.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-NO-VALID
      10.12. No Valid Rerank Candidates GHOST-DOC-RERANK-NO-VALID Real reranking shall fail explicitly when no candidate can be prepared for ColBERT scoring.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-ENCODE
      11.1. ColBERT Encoding GHOST-DOC-RERANK-ENCODE Real reranking shall encode query pieces as queries and the cleaned candidate snippets as documents using the configured ColBERT model.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-DOCS-PER-QUERY
        11.2. Candidate Set per Query Piece GHOST-DOC-RERANK-DOCS-PER-QUERY Every query piece shall be scored against the same ordered valid candidate identifier and document list.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-MEAN
        11.3. ColBERT Piece Aggregation GHOST-DOC-RERANK-MEAN For each chunk identifier, ColBERT scores returned across query pieces shall be aggregated by arithmetic mean.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-COLBERT-SORT
        11.4. ColBERT Deterministic Sort GHOST-DOC-RERANK-COLBERT-SORT Aggregated ColBERT rows shall be ordered by descending mean score and ascending chunk identifier for ties.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-RRF2
      11.5. Second Weighted RRF GHOST-DOC-RERANK-RRF2 Reranker shall fuse the original retrieval ranking with the ColBERT ranking through the same neutral weighted RRF helper.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-WEIGHTS
        11.6. Current Reranker Fusion Weights GHOST-DOC-RERANK-WEIGHTS The current second-fusion baseline shall weight Retrieval 0.75 and ColBERT 0.25.

        Comments describing equal weighting shall not override the executed values.
        • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-WEIGHTS
          14.13. AC: Executed Weight Truth GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-WEIGHTS The effective retrieval and reranking weights reported for the current baseline shall be 0.75/0.25 unless validated JSON configuration overrides them in implemented code.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-META-PRESERVE
        11.7. Retrieval Metadata Preservation GHOST-DOC-RERANK-META-PRESERVE Before the second fusion overwrites generic rrf_score, the original retrieval fused score shall be preserved under retrieval_rrf_score when available.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-META-PROJECT
        11.8. Reranker Metadata Projection GHOST-DOC-RERANK-META-PROJECT Reranker shall project neutral second-fusion fields to retrieval_score, colbert_score, retrieval_rank, colbert_rank, and rerank_rrf_score.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-WRITE-META
        11.9. Chunk Metadata Write-Back GHOST-DOC-RERANK-WRITE-META Reranker-specific scores and ranks shall be merged into the hydrated chunk metadata for later diagnostic rendering.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-FINAL-SORT
        11.10. Final Rerank Order GHOST-DOC-RERANK-FINAL-SORT The final reranked rows shall be sorted by descending rerank fused score and ascending chunk identifier for ties.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-COLBERT
        14.10. AC: ColBERT Reranking GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-COLBERT Given real reranking enabled and valid candidates, ColBERT mean scores shall be fused with retrieval ranking using the configured second-fusion values and shall produce the reranked view.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-BYPASS
      12.1. ColBERT Bypass GHOST-DOC-RERANK-BYPASS When use_reranking_colbert is false, Reranker shall copy the bounded retrieval order and scores into the reranked stage without calling the ColBERT model.
      • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-BYPASS-META
        12.2. Bypass Metadata GHOST-DOC-RERANK-BYPASS-META Bypass may populate retrieval and ColBERT score/rank aliases from the retrieval order solely to preserve downstream metadata shape; diagnostics shall identify the bypass.
      • GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-RERANK-BYPASS
        14.11. AC: ColBERT Bypass GHOST-DOC-RETRIEVE-AC-RERANK-BYPASS Given ColBERT disabled, no ColBERT model call shall occur and retrieval order shall be copied into the reranked stage.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-VIEW
      12.3. Reranked View GHOST-DOC-RERANK-VIEW sp.views_by_stage["reranked"] shall contain ordered chunk identifier, effective rerank score, and SELECTED status for every retained candidate.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-IDS
      12.4. Reranked Final IDs GHOST-DOC-RERANK-IDS sp.final_selection_ids shall equal the ordered identifiers in the reranked view.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-STAGE
      12.5. Reranker Lifecycle GHOST-DOC-RERANK-STAGE After real or bypass reranking, sp.stage shall equal reranked and history_of_stages shall receive reranked.
    • GHOST-DOC-RERANK-BASE-PRESERVE
      12.6. Base Chunk Preservation GHOST-DOC-RERANK-BASE-PRESERVE Reranker shall not replace base_context_chunks; it shall reorder candidates through views and selection identifiers while enriching metadata only.
